# :contains() selector doesn't work with identifiers ## Description I found that the `:contains()` selector doesn't work properly when using identifiers instead of strings. For example: ```python from pyquery import PyQuery as pq # This works fine html = pq('

test

') result1 = html('p:contains("test")') print(result1) # Outputs:

test

# This doesn't work html = pq('

test

') result2 = html('p:contains(test)') # Using identifier instead of string print(result2) # Outputs nothing ``` According to jQuery documentation, the `:contains()` selector should work with both string literals and identifiers, but in pyquery it only works with string literals. I also tried with non-ASCII characters and got the same issue: ```python html = pq('

é

') print(html('p:contains("é")')) # Works print(html('p:contains(é)')) # Doesn't work ``` This is inconsistent with jQuery's behavior where both forms should work. It makes it harder to port jQuery code to pyquery.
I'll inspect the repository and locate how `:contains()` is implemented so we can fix identifier handling.
